task_text: Search the EO Dashboard for the narrative on the 2019–2020 Australian bushfires. Identify the affected study area, select an appropriate Earth observation dataset for mapping burn scars, retrieve data covering the region, and explain why the chosen dataset is suitable and how it relates to the narrative.

criteria.description: The answer scientifically justifies the chosen dataset for mapping fire effects over the selected area and period, accurately describing its relevant capabilities and limitations—for example, MODIS burned-area and burn-date information for broad coverage or Sentinel-2 NBR for burn-related spectral contrast when coverage is adequately tiled.

The answer identifies a defensible affected study area, describes the retrieved data's actual spatial and temporal coverage or evidence without inventing unsupported patterns, and explains how that evidence relates to the 2019–2020 bushfire narrative.

The answer's suitability rationale and conclusions follow from the data it says it retrieved, with no contradictions between the selected area, dataset capabilities, observed evidence, and claims about the bushfires.

task_text: Download a Sentinel-2 RGB satellite image of central Rome, Italy for the period January to March 2023, at 10 m resolution with less than 20% cloud cover. Is the Tiber River clearly visible? If so, describe the direction in which it flows across the image.

criteria.description: The answer gives a scientifically defensible assessment of whether the Tiber is discernible in the requested true-color imagery and, if it is, accurately describes its flow direction rather than confusing flow direction with the river's visible alignment.

The answer makes an image-specific visibility judgment and, when applicable, describes the river's direction across the central-Rome Sentinel-2 RGB scene for January–March 2023 at 10 m resolution and less than 20% cloud cover.
The answer's visibility conclusion, directional description, and any qualifications are mutually consistent and follow from the visual evidence it describes.

task_text: Find an EOdashboard narrative about environmental changes observed from space during the Covid-19 lockdown (such as improved air quality, clearer waterways, or reduced maritime traffic), identify the affected study area, then download two Sentinel-2 true-colour images of that area — one from approximately one year before the lockdown (same season, 2019) and one from during the lockdown (2020) — and compare the two images to assess whether visible environmental changes are apparent.

criteria.description: Interpret visible differences in the Sentinel-2 true-colour imagery in ways the imagery can support, distinguishing observed appearance from claims about causes or broader environmental trends that the images alone cannot establish.

Identify the affected study area from an EOdashboard lockdown narrative and compare evidence from the requested same-season 2019 and lockdown-period 2020 images, describing whether visible environmental changes are apparent rather than giving a generic account.
Ensure the stated comparison and conclusions follow from the observations described and do not contradict the answer’s account of the study area, images, or visible changes.

task_text: Download a true-colour Sentinel-2 satellite image of central Barcelona, Spain for July 2022 at 10 m resolution with a maximum cloud cover of 15%. Inspect the image and assess whether urban structures, roads, and built-up areas are clearly visible. Explain whether the image is suitable for urban feature mapping.

criteria.description: Claims about what the July 2022 true-colour Sentinel-2 image at 10 m resolution can reveal, and whether it supports urban feature mapping, are scientifically defensible and appropriately account for the limits of the image.

The answer addresses the specified central Barcelona image context and gives image-specific observations about the visibility of urban structures, roads, and built-up areas to support its suitability assessment, rather than relying on generic claims.
The suitability conclusion follows logically from the visual evidence described, and the answer does not make contradictory claims about feature visibility or mapping capability.

task_text: Download a false-colour near-infrared composite of the agricultural area around Cremona, Lombardy, Italy for the growing season (June–August 2021) at 20 m resolution. Describe the spatial patterns of vegetation conditions visible in the image and identify areas with stronger or weaker vegetation signals.

criteria.description: Interprets the false-colour near-infrared signal as a relative indication of vegetation response, using the composite's band display appropriately and avoiding unsupported claims that signal strength alone proves crop health, yield, or cause.

Describes spatial patterns visible in the June–August 2021, 20 m imagery of the agricultural area around Cremona and identifies where vegetation signals appear relatively stronger or weaker, grounding those distinctions in the image rather than giving a generic account.
Presents a coherent account in which the stated visual evidence supports the stronger-versus-weaker vegetation comparisons and any interpretation of those comparisons.

task_text: Find an EO Dashboard narrative about forest cover change, identify the study area and time period it discusses, and retrieve a Sentinel-2 true-colour image covering that area. Describe whether the retrieved imagery provides visible evidence supporting the forest cover changes reported in the narrative.

criteria.description: The answer interprets visible land-cover features in the Sentinel-2 true-colour image scientifically and does not claim that a single image alone establishes forest-cover change over time.

The answer identifies the selected EO Dashboard narrative's study area and stated time period, establishes that the retrieved Sentinel-2 true-colour image covers that area, and describes artifact-specific evidence relevant to the narrative's forest-change claim.

The answer's judgment about whether the image supports the narrative follows logically from the visible evidence it reports and is consistent with the spatial and temporal relationship it describes between the image and narrative.

task_text: Find an EO Dashboard narrative about forest habitat change, extract a study area from it, and download a Sentinel-2 true-colour image for that area for the most recent available year. Identify whether the selected area still appears to contain the forest habitat described in the dashboard and explain your reasoning.

criteria.description: The answer interprets visible features in the selected Sentinel-2 true-colour image in a scientifically defensible way, distinguishing apparent forest cover from stronger claims about habitat quality, ecological condition, or change that the image alone cannot establish.

The answer identifies the dashboard narrative and its study area, specifies the most recent available year of the assessed Sentinel-2 image, and answers whether the described forest habitat appears present using evidence observable in that image.
The answer’s conclusion about whether forest habitat appears present follows logically from the visual evidence it describes, with no contradictions between its image observations and interpretation.

task_text: Download a Sentinel-2 image with bands B8 and B4 for the area around Ciudad Real in central Spain during the summer drought period of July–September 2022 at 10 m resolution, then find EO Dashboard narratives that discuss food security or extreme climate impacts relevant to agricultural drought in Europe.

criteria.description: Scientific claims correctly characterize Sentinel-2 B8 as near-infrared and B4 as red, and do not treat this imagery or a narrative reference alone as proof of drought causation, food insecurity, or long-term change.

The answer grounds its account in an image for the Ciudad Real area from July–September 2022 using B8 and B4 at 10 m resolution, and identifies at least one actual EO Dashboard narrative relevant to European agricultural drought through food security or extreme climate impacts.

The answer's descriptions of the image, its dates, bands, resolution, and the relevance of the identified narrative(s) are mutually consistent, and its conclusions follow from the evidence it presents.

task_text: Retrieve multiple priority areas from the ESA Earth Observation Science Strategy, identify the related Earth observation application domains, and search for MOOC lectures covering satellite-based monitoring methods for each domain. Determine which ESA priorities are represented in the available MOOC content, and explain how the lectures support the corresponding strategy objectives.

criteria.description: Correctly relates each selected ESA priority to an appropriate Earth observation application domain and explains how the cited satellite-monitoring methods can support the priority’s objectives without overstating what the methods establish.

Identifies multiple ESA priorities, their related application domains, and relevant MOOC lecture content, accurately stating which selected priorities are represented and explaining the connection between the lectures and the strategy objectives using evidence from the strategy and catalogue.
Keeps the priority-to-domain mappings, reported MOOC coverage, and conclusions about how the lectures support the objectives logically consistent with the evidence presented.

task_text: Find an EO Dashboard narrative about glaciers or cryosphere change. Extract the study area discussed, then download the corresponding data using the appropriate data access tool. Summarize what the downloaded data reveals about the cryosphere conditions or ice extent described in the narrative and explain your reasoning.

criteria.description: Interpret the selected EO data in a scientifically defensible way for assessing cryosphere conditions, distinguishing observable snow or ice from stronger claims such as glacier change when the data do not support them.

Identify the study area from an EO Dashboard glacier or cryosphere narrative and describe specific evidence in the corresponding downloaded data that bears on the cryosphere conditions or ice extent discussed there.
Ensure the conclusions about cryosphere conditions or ice extent follow from the evidence and reasoning presented and are consistent with the stated study area, data, and narrative context.

task_text: Find two separate EO Dashboard narratives related to greenhouse gas monitoring: one focused on carbon emissions or carbon storage, and one focused on other greenhouse gases such as methane or atmospheric pollutants. Identify the study areas discussed in each narrative, retrieve the relevant satellite datasets, and summarize their spatial resolution, temporal coverage, measured variables, and relevance for monitoring the emissions described in the narratives.

criteria.description: Accurately explains what each selected satellite dataset measures and how it can inform monitoring of the emissions described, distinguishing direct measurements from proxies and qualifying limitations where relevant.

Grounds the account in two separate EO Dashboard narratives—one about carbon emissions or storage and one about other greenhouse gases or atmospheric pollutants—identifies each study area, and reports the relevant dataset's spatial resolution, temporal coverage, measured variables, and monitoring relevance without requiring a particular sensor or dataset.

Presents conclusions about each study area and its emissions consistently with the dataset characteristics and evidence described, without making unsupported claims about what the observations establish.

task_text: Find an EO Dashboard narrative about climate change impacts, retrieve its full content to identify the study area, select and download an appropriate EO image for that area, and query the ESA Science Strategy for policy context on the same topic. Explain how the selected observation helps assess the climate impact described in the narrative.

criteria.description: The answer accurately explains how the chosen EO observation can provide evidence relevant to the climate impact described, while avoiding claims that the selected data cannot scientifically establish.

The answer grounds its account in the retrieved narrative and selected observation, identifies the narrative’s study area and climate-impact topic, and includes relevant ESA Science Strategy policy context.
The answer’s explanation of the observation’s relevance and limitations follows from the evidence it presents and is consistent with its account of the narrative and policy context.

task_text: Find an EO Dashboard narrative about greenhouse gas emissions from industrial activity. Identify the study area mentioned in the narrative, retrieve a suitable methane observation dataset (such as Sentinel-5P or another atmospheric composition product) for that location, and search for ESA educational resources on satellite monitoring of greenhouse gases. Explain how the retrieved observations relate to the emissions issue discussed in the narrative.

criteria.description: The answer correctly characterizes its chosen methane observation product and interprets what it measures, avoiding unsupported claims that an atmospheric methane observation alone quantifies or attributes emissions to a particular industrial source.

The answer identifies the study area named in the selected EO Dashboard narrative, describes evidence from the retrieved methane observations for that area, and identifies an ESA educational resource relevant to satellite greenhouse-gas monitoring.

The answer's explanation of how the retrieved observations relate to the narrative's industrial emissions issue follows from the evidence it presents and is consistent with its stated limitations and conclusions.

task_text: Download two Sentinel-2 true-colour images of Bordeaux, France — one before the July 2022 heatwave and wildfires (April–June 2022) and one after (August–September 2022) — to assess landscape changes caused by the extreme weather event. Compare the two images and assess whether visible landscape changes — such as vegetation stress, burn scars, or browning — are observable between the pre- and post-event periods.

criteria.description: Scientifically interprets the Sentinel-2 true-colour imagery as evidence of visible surface appearance, and does not treat a before-and-after comparison alone as proof that any observed change was caused by the heatwave or wildfires.

Compares the Bordeaux images from April–June and August–September 2022, describing image-supported visible changes or their absence and addressing whether signs such as vegetation stress, burn scars, or browning are observable.
Draws a conclusion about visible landscape change that follows consistently from the evidence and comparison described in the answer.

task_text: Find an EO Dashboard narrative related to food security and crop monitoring. Identify the agricultural region discussed in the narrative, retrieve a MODIS NDVI vegetation-index product covering that area, and identify relevant ESA Earth Observation Science Strategy objectives and educational resources on satellite-based crop monitoring. Explain how the NDVI observations and supporting resources relate to the crop-monitoring objectives described in the narrative.

criteria.description: The answer correctly treats MODIS NDVI as an indicator of vegetation greenness or crop condition relevant to monitoring, and does not present NDVI alone as a direct measurement of crop yield, food security, or causal change.

The answer identifies the agricultural region discussed in the selected food-security or crop-monitoring narrative, grounds its account in MODIS NDVI observations covering that region, identifies relevant ESA Earth Observation Science Strategy objectives and satellite crop-monitoring educational resources, and relates these to the narrative's monitoring objectives.

The answer's explanation of how the NDVI observations and supporting strategy and educational resources serve the narrative's crop-monitoring objectives follows coherently from the evidence and qualifications it presents.

task_text: Find the EO Dashboard narrative about air pollution changes, identify a representative city discussed in the narrative, and retrieve a Sentinel-5P atmospheric composition product for that location. Inspect the retrieved data and describe the spatial distribution of the pollutant signal (e.g., NO₂ concentration), explaining how it relates to the air-quality changes described in the narrative.

criteria.description: Interpret the selected Sentinel-5P atmospheric-composition signal using scientifically appropriate terms and limitations (for example, treating a NO₂ column product as column abundance rather than a direct ground-level concentration measurement), and avoid unsupported causal or long-term claims from the observation.

Identify the air-pollution narrative and a defensible representative city, describe the pollutant’s spatial distribution as supported by the retrieved product, and relate that evidence to the air-quality changes described in the narrative without inventing artifact-specific patterns or values.

Ensure that the reported spatial pattern, its interpretation, and the stated relationship to the narrative are logically compatible with one another and with the observation’s temporal and spatial scope.

task_text: Find the EO Dashboard narrative about using satellites to monitor land cover and aboveground biomass, identify the study region it discusses, and retrieve the MODIS annual land-cover product covering that area. Summarize the dominant land-cover classes and explain how they relate to the biomass monitoring described in the narrative.

criteria.description: Scientifically interprets the reported MODIS land-cover classes and explains their relevance to monitoring aboveground biomass without treating land-cover class alone as a direct biomass measurement.

Identifies the EO Dashboard land-cover and biomass narrative, names a defensible study region it covers, identifies the annual MODIS land-cover product used for that region, and summarizes dominant classes supported by the retrieved product.
Keeps the stated region, land-cover summary, and explanation of biomass monitoring mutually consistent, with conclusions that follow from the evidence presented.

task_text: Find the EO Dashboard narrative about COVID-19 travel restrictions disrupting global cargo shipping, identify a representative shipping chokepoint, and retrieve Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 imagery for that location. Use the SAR data to assess maritime activity and the optical image to describe the surrounding port infrastructure and geographic context.

criteria.description: Scientifically interprets maritime activity from features visible in Sentinel-1 SAR and describes port infrastructure and geographic context visible in Sentinel-2 optical imagery, without treating either image alone as proof of vessel counts, long-term change, or COVID-related causation.

Identifies the relevant EO Dashboard cargo-shipping disruption narrative, selects a defensible representative global shipping chokepoint, and gives artifact-specific observations from both imagery types that address the requested maritime-activity and surrounding-context assessments.

Keeps its conclusions about the chokepoint, maritime activity, and surrounding infrastructure logically aligned with the evidence it describes, and distinguishes image-based observations from any broader claims about global shipping disruption.

task_text: Retrieve a Sentinel-2 true-colour image of central Wuhan, Hubei, China during the February 2020 COVID-19 lockdown period. Select the most suitable available acquisition based on cloud cover and image quality. Describe the visible urban environment and explain what information can and cannot be inferred from this optical image about lockdown-related changes.

criteria.description: Correctly explains that a Sentinel-2 true-colour image can show visible surface features but, by itself, cannot establish lockdown-related changes in human activity or attribute observed conditions to the lockdown without suitable comparative evidence.

Grounds the account in the selected February 2020 Sentinel-2 true-colour scene of central Wuhan by explaining its suitability in terms of observed image quality or cloud conditions and describing urban features actually discernible in the image.
Presents conclusions about the scene and lockdown-related inferences that follow logically from the visual evidence and limitations stated, without contradicting its own description.

task_text: Retrieve a false-colour near-infrared composite of the agricultural area near Mansoura, Egypt for March–April 2022 at 20 m resolution. Describe the main vegetation patterns visible in the image before harvest.

criteria.description: Interprets the selected near-infrared false-colour composite scientifically, treating displayed colours and brightness as indicators of vegetation reflectance or cover rather than literal surface colours or definitive proof of crop identity, condition, or harvest status.

Describes image-specific spatial patterns and variation in vegetation across the agricultural area near Mansoura during March–April 2022, addressing the requested pre-harvest view rather than offering only generic statements about agriculture.
Keeps its description of the visible vegetation patterns, its interpretation of the false-colour evidence, and any conclusions about pre-harvest conditions logically consistent with one another.

task_text: Download a true-colour Sentinel-2 image of the area around Darmstadt, Germany — home to ESA's European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) and EUMETSAT headquarters — for July 2022. Estimate the proportion of built-up versus vegetated land cover and describe the spatial distribution of green space relative to the urban core.

criteria.description: Interprets built-up and vegetated cover in the July 2022 true-colour Sentinel-2 image as visual land-cover estimates, avoiding unsupported precision or claims that the image alone cannot establish.

Provides approximate built-up and vegetated proportions and describes the observed distribution of green space relative to Darmstadt’s urban core, grounding both in the requested image rather than generic assumptions.
Keeps the estimated land-cover proportions, the description of green-space distribution, and the overall interpretation mutually consistent and supported by the evidence it presents.

task_text: Find the EO Dashboard narrative about extreme air pollution episodes in Northern India and Pakistan, identify a representative city discussed in the narrative, and retrieve Sentinel-5P atmospheric composition data for that location during the smog season. Describe the spatial distribution of pollutant concentrations and explain how the observations relate to the pollution episode described in the narrative.

criteria.description: Scientifically interprets the selected Sentinel-5P atmospheric-composition measurement and its spatial pattern, distinguishing the measured pollutant or quantity from overall air pollution and avoiding unsupported claims about cause or exposure.

Identifies the pollution narrative and a representative city in the Northern India–Pakistan region, then describes the observed pollutant distribution in a suitable smog-season product for that location and relates the evidence to the episode.

Keeps the stated location, observation period, measured quantity, described spatial pattern, and connection to the narrative mutually consistent, with conclusions proportionate to the evidence presented.

task_text: Find an EO Dashboard narrative about climate change effects on ocean warming, identify a representative coastal study area and the relevant time period discussed in the narrative, and retrieve a JAXA daily sea surface temperature (SST) product for that region. To avoid downloading the full time series, select representative observations from the period of interest (e.g., one observation per year during the same season if the period spans multiple years). Describe the observed SST patterns and explain how they relate to the ocean warming impacts described in the narrative.

criteria.description: Interpret the selected JAXA daily SST observations in a scientifically defensible way, relating relevant SST conditions to the narrative's ocean-warming impacts without treating a few representative seasonal snapshots alone as proof of a long-term trend or causal mechanism.

Identify the relevant EO Dashboard narrative, a representative coastal study area and the narrative's period of interest, then describe observed SST patterns from JAXA daily SST data for that area and period and explain their relevance to the described impacts, using comparable seasonal samples if multiple years are represented.
Ensure that the stated SST patterns, dates, comparisons, and conclusions are mutually consistent and that the interpretation follows from the observations and limitations described in the answer.

task_text: Download a Sentinel-2 true-colour image of the coastal area near Cairns, Queensland, Australia for September 2022 at 10 m resolution. Then find an EO Dashboard narrative about climate change effects on ocean warming in the same region. Describe whether the image provides visible context supporting the impacts discussed in the narrative.

criteria.description: Scientifically distinguishes visible features in a September 2022 Sentinel-2 true-colour image from ocean warming and its climate impacts, without treating a single optical image as a direct measurement of warming or proof of its causes.

Grounds the assessment in the actual 10 m Cairns-area image and a relevant EO Dashboard narrative about climate-change effects on ocean warming in the same region, describing whether visible features provide context for the impacts discussed rather than giving a generic account.
Draws a conclusion about whether the image provides supporting context that follows from the visible evidence it describes and is consistent with the narrative’s stated impacts.

task_text: Find an EO Dashboard narrative about land cover change or urbanisation. Read the full content to identify the study area and the main change process described. Retrieve a Sentinel-2 image covering that area for 2023 using an appropriate false-colour composite. Describe the visible land-cover patterns and assess whether the image provides evidence consistent with the changes reported in the narrative.

criteria.description: Correctly interprets visible land-cover patterns in the selected appropriate Sentinel-2 false-colour composite and appropriately qualifies what a single 2023 image can establish about the narrative's reported change.

Identifies the study area and main change process from the chosen EO Dashboard narrative, describes spatial patterns actually visible in the retrieved 2023 image, and assesses their relevance to that process without inventing unsupported details.

Presents a conclusion about whether the image is consistent with the narrative that logically follows from the described image evidence and does not contradict its own account of the data or limitations.

task_text: Search the EO Dashboard for a narrative about deforestation or forest loss. Identify a representative area of documented forest loss, then download two Sentinel-2 true-colour images of that area: one before and one after the reported forest change. Compare the images and describe visible land-cover changes.

criteria.description: Interprets the Sentinel-2 true-colour images as evidence of visible land-cover differences, such as reduced forest canopy or new clearings, without treating imagery alone as proof of a specific cause or broader long-term trend.

Identifies a representative area associated with a forest-loss narrative and describes a comparison grounded in two Sentinel-2 true-colour images of that area, one before and one after the reported change.
Ensures the described land-cover changes and conclusions are consistent with the stated before-and-after evidence and do not contradict the answer's own account of the images.

task_text: Search the EO Dashboard for narratives about wildfires or burned areas. Identify the study area they discuss, then download two Sentinel-2 false-colour near-infrared composites of the affected area: one before and one after the wildfire event. Compare the images and describe visible changes in vegetation cover, burned areas, and landscape conditions associated with the fire.

criteria.description: Scientifically interprets the Sentinel-2 false-colour near-infrared composites, describing visible vegetation or burn-related signals accurately and avoiding claims about fire effects that the imagery cannot establish.

Identifies the study area discussed in a wildfire or burned-area narrative and grounds a before-and-after comparison of that affected area in the two composites, addressing visible vegetation cover, burned areas, and landscape conditions.
Ensures that the stated changes and conclusions follow from the comparison presented and are consistent with the images’ pre-fire and post-fire ordering.

task_text: Search the EO Dashboard for a narrative about Amazon deforestation. Read the complete narrative to identify the study area and environmental issue discussed. Download the relevant satellite assets: select a Sentinel-2 false-colour image covering the same region during the dry season (July–September 2022). Summarize the visible evidence of deforestation or forest degradation and explain how it supports or challenges the findings described in the narrative.

criteria.description: Interpret the selected Sentinel-2 false-colour image in a scientifically defensible way, treating visible clearing or forest degradation patterns as evidence while avoiding unsupported claims about change, cause, or ecological condition that the image alone cannot establish.

Identify the study area and environmental issue from the narrative, describe spatially specific evidence actually visible in the same-region July–September 2022 image, and state whether that evidence supports or challenges the narrative’s findings.
Ensure that the stated support-or-challenge conclusion follows from the described image evidence and narrative findings, with any differences in spatial or temporal scope handled consistently.

task_text: Search the ESA Science Strategy for priorities on glacier and cryosphere monitoring and search MOOC content for lectures on ice sheet remote sensing. Identify a glacier or cryosphere study site relevant to these sources, download a recent summer Sentinel-2 image of that location, and describe the visible cryosphere features that are relevant for monitoring climate change impacts.

criteria.description: Correctly identifies and interprets cryosphere features visible in the selected summer Sentinel-2 image as relevant to climate-impact monitoring, using scientifically defensible claims appropriate to the image and its resolution.

Grounds its account in the selected study site and downloaded image, and identifies relevant ESA Science Strategy priorities and MOOC content on ice-sheet remote sensing without substituting generic material for the sources or imagery.

Presents conclusions that follow from the described image evidence and appropriately distinguishes what a single summer image can show from longer-term change or causal claims it cannot establish on its own.

task_text: Find what the ESA Science Strategy says about monitoring carbon emissions from space, then search arXiv for papers published in the last year on satellite-based carbon or CO₂ monitoring. Compare the research priorities in the strategy with the approaches described in recent papers — identify areas of alignment and any gaps.

criteria.description: Accurately represents the relevant ESA Science Strategy priorities and the methods and capabilities described in the selected papers, distinguishing satellite-observed greenhouse-gas concentrations from emissions or fluxes inferred using additional methods where relevant.

Grounds the comparison in identifiable arXiv papers from the requested last-year period and specific strategy priorities, and explains at least one evidence-based area of alignment and one gap between them.
Ensures that the stated alignments, gaps, and overall conclusions follow from the strategy priorities and paper approaches the answer describes, without contradicting its own evidence.

task_text: Look up what the ESA Science Strategy says about cryosphere monitoring and sea ice observations, then search arXiv for recent papers on Arctic sea ice remote sensing. Assess whether the current research literature addresses the strategy's stated priorities — highlight commonalities and any under-explored areas.

criteria.description: Accurately represents the ESA Science Strategy’s stated cryosphere and sea-ice priorities and scientifically interprets the relevance and capabilities of the recent Arctic sea-ice remote-sensing research discussed, without overstating what the observations or papers establish.

Bases the comparison on identifiable evidence from the strategy and the recent arXiv search, and addresses both areas of alignment and potentially under-explored priorities while making clear that the assessment is limited to the literature searched.

Draws conclusions about commonalities and research gaps that follow from the strategy priorities and paper evidence presented, without treating limited search results as proof that a topic is absent from the broader literature.

task_text: Find what the ESA Science Strategy says about water resources management and hydrological monitoring, then search arXiv for recent papers on satellite hydrology or soil moisture retrieval and retrieve the abstract of the top result. Compare the strategy's priorities with the paper's focus — note where they converge and where gaps remain.

criteria.description: Accurately represents the ESA Science Strategy’s stated priorities for water resources management and hydrological monitoring and the selected paper’s focus, without attributing unsupported claims or treating the paper as evidence of more than its abstract supports.

Bases the comparison on identifiable content from the ESA strategy and the retrieved abstract of the recent top-result arXiv paper, and explains both where their priorities and focus converge and where gaps remain.
Draws conclusions about convergence and gaps that follow from the evidence presented and remains consistent in describing the strategy’s priorities and the paper’s scope.

task_text: Look up the ESA Science Strategy's position on disaster risk reduction and emergency response using satellite data, then search arXiv for recent papers on flood or earthquake damage assessment from satellite imagery and build the citation graph of the top result. Assess how well the recent literature addresses the strategy's disaster response priorities, noting areas of overlap and divergence.

criteria.description: Accurately characterizes the ESA Science Strategy’s position on disaster risk reduction and emergency response, and makes scientifically defensible claims about how satellite observations can support the selected flood- or earthquake-damage assessment without overstating what the data establish.

Addresses the strategy’s relevant priorities, the selected recent arXiv satellite-imagery damage-assessment paper and its citation graph, and explicitly assesses areas of overlap and divergence using claims supported by the retrieved materials without requiring a particular paper, sensor, method, or finding.

Presents conclusions about how the paper and citation graph address the strategy that follow logically from the evidence and reasoning given, with no material contradictions among its descriptions, comparisons, and conclusions.

task_text: Find out what the ESA Science Strategy says about solid Earth deformation and land subsidence in urban environments, then search arXiv for recent papers on InSAR-based urban subsidence or land deformation monitoring from satellite data. Compare the scale and focus of the research literature with the strategy's urban deformation monitoring objectives — identify what the community is actively pursuing versus what the strategy emphasises.

criteria.description: Accurately characterizes the ESA Science Strategy’s relevant objectives for solid-Earth deformation and urban land subsidence, and describes the arXiv papers’ InSAR or other satellite-based deformation research without scientifically unsupported claims.

Grounds the comparison in the strategy content and recent arXiv papers actually retrieved, addressing their respective scale and focus and identifying both the research themes represented in the paper sample and the objectives emphasized by the strategy.

Draws conclusions that follow from the evidence presented, distinguishes strategic objectives from the topics represented in the searched paper sample, and does not treat that sample as a complete measure of all community research.

task_text: Download a Sentinel-2 image of the agricultural area around Zinder, Niger for July-September 2022 with bands B3, B4, and B8, all at native 10 m resolution. Compute NDVI and NDWI, save the results, report raster statistics for each index, and state whether the statistics indicate dense, dry vegetation or a wetter, water-influenced landscape across the study area.

criteria.description: Computes the requested indices using scientifically valid formulas for the supplied bands—NDVI = (B8 − B4)/(B8 + B4) and green–NIR NDWI = (B3 − B8)/(B3 + B8)—and treats them as spectral indicators rather than direct proof of ecological conditions.

Identifies the analysis as based on the requested July–September 2022, native-10 m B3/B4/B8 Sentinel-2 imagery for the agricultural area around Zinder, indicates that both index results were saved, and reports artifact-derived minimum, mean, and maximum statistics for each index.

Clearly states whether the reported statistics support dense, dry vegetation or a wetter, water-influenced landscape, and makes that judgment consistent with the reported NDVI and NDWI values and their spatial summaries.

task_text: Download a Sentinel-2 image of the area around Córdoba, Andalusia, Spain for the summer drought period of July-September 2022 with bands B4, B8, and B11 at 10-20 m resolution. Compute NDVI and NDMI, save the resulting rasters, and produce 256-bin histograms of both indices to assess vegetation condition and drought-related moisture stress.

criteria.description: Correctly identifies NDVI as (B8 − B4)/(B8 + B4) and NDMI as (B8 − B11)/(B8 + B11), and interprets them as indicators of vegetation greenness and canopy moisture, respectively, without treating either index alone as definitive proof of drought causation.

Describes the Córdoba-area Sentinel-2 observation for July–September 2022 using B4, B8, and B11 at the requested 10–20 m resolution, and reports artifact-specific evidence from both saved index rasters and their 256-bin histograms to assess vegetation condition and moisture stress.

Ensures that the vegetation and moisture-stress conclusions follow from the histogram or raster evidence presented and that claims about the observation, indices, and drought interpretation do not contradict one another.

task_text: Find an EO Dashboard narrative about satellite-based agricultural monitoring, identify the key farming region discussed, and retrieve a MODIS NDVI vegetation-index product covering that area. Visualize the NDVI product and describe the spatial patterns of vegetation activity, identifying areas of higher and lower vegetation response. Explain how these patterns relate to the agricultural conditions described in the narrative.

criteria.description: Interprets NDVI as a proxy for vegetation greenness or activity and draws scientifically defensible agricultural conclusions for the selected region and observation period without treating NDVI alone as a direct measure of yield or proof of causation.

Identifies a defensible farming region relevant to the agricultural-monitoring narrative, describes image-supported areas of relatively higher and lower vegetation response in a MODIS NDVI visualization covering that region, and relates the observed pattern to the narrative’s crop-monitoring discussion.
Presents conclusions that follow from the spatial evidence and reasoning given, with no contradictions among the selected region, described NDVI patterns, and agricultural interpretation.

task_text: Find an EO Dashboard narrative about forest loss and changing forest landscapes, identify the study area discussed, and retrieve a MODIS surface-reflectance product covering that region. Describe the regional-scale vegetation patterns visible in the imagery and explain how they relate to the forest changes described in the narrative.

criteria.description: Scientifically interprets the vegetation patterns visible in the selected MODIS surface-reflectance imagery and relates them plausibly to forest loss or landscape change, without treating a single image as proof of a long-term trend or cause.
